fills.reason: Looked for shared-storage APIs and storage permissions. The app uses only getExternalFilesDir (app-specific external dir, used as default backup/attachment location) and MediaStore intents delegated to camera/recorder apps; no WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE or MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared, so the permission condition of the test is not met.

Looked for SecretKeySpec or byte-array keys in Android code. The only key used on Android is generated inside AndroidKeyStore by AndroidKeyProvider; KeyStoreEncryption takes it from the provider. The SecretKeySpec in DesktopKeyProvider is desktop-only code, not in the APK.

Release builds plant a FileLogger (Timber DebugTree, all priorities) and the Microsoft Graph client logs HTTP HEADERS in release via Timber.d. Authorization is sanitized, but Cookie/Set-Cookie headers are not; logs go to cacheDir and can be exported with logcat in a support zip. Whether those Graph cookies are session-sensitive needs a human decision.

evidence.detail: Release builds log request/response headers of the Graph client; only Authorization is sanitized.

fills.reason: No WebView, WebSettings or setJavaScriptEnabled in any Kotlin/Java source of the app modules (grep over app, kmp, composeApp, cert4android, wear).
No WebView or setAllowFileAccess* calls anywhere in the app's sources.
No WebView or addJavascriptInterface anywhere in the app's sources.
No WebView or onReceivedSslError override in the app's sources.
No WebView and no setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled call in the app's sources.
No WebView/WebViewClient, shouldOverrideUrlLoading or shouldInterceptRequest in the app's sources.
No WebView in the app, and no EnableSafeBrowsing meta-data in any manifest.
Looked at the credential input fields (CalDAV and EteSync password fields); both use KeyboardType.Password with PasswordVisualTransformation. Other text fields hold task content, not credentials.

Password entry fields in CalDAV and EteSync sign-in use PasswordVisualTransformation, so input is masked. The generated app-password dialog shows a server-issued password on purpose (covered under screenshot and clipboard checks).
No FLAG_SECURE, setSecure or setRecentsScreenshotEnabled anywhere in the app, yet the Tasks.org account screen shows a newly generated app password in clear text.

evidence.detail: Generated app password is displayed in a dialog with no screenshot protection.

fills.reason: No filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED checks or setHideOverlayWindows anywhere, while the app has credential sign-in screens (CalDAV, EteSync) and a certificate-trust screen.

evidence.detail: Credential entry field with no overlay/tapjacking protection.

fills.reason: minSdk is 26 and reminder notifications show the task title and description with no lock-screen visibility (setVisibility/setPublicVersion is never used). Whether users' task content counts as sensitive is a product decision.

evidence.detail: Task title is shown in the reminder notification, public on the lock screen by default.

fills.reason: Internal broadcasts go through androidx LocalBroadcastManager (in-process) or use explicit components (CompleteTaskReceiver, TasksWidget); PendingIntents wrap explicit intents. No implicit intent for internal communication was found.

Task titles and details are sent to the Pebble companion app through PebbleKit.sendDataToPebbleWithTransactionId, which dispatches a broadcast from library code; whether the library restricts the recipient package can't be seen in the app's sources.

evidence.detail: Task data handed to PebbleKit's broadcast-based transport.

fills.reason: Every PendingIntent wraps an explicit intent. FLAG_MUTABLE (or the pre-S mutable default) is only used where the system or a library must fill in the intent: AppAuth completion, geofence/location callbacks, the widget collection template and requestPinAppWidget callbacks. The pinned-shortcut callback is immutable and has no action, so it can't resolve to another app.
No intent-filter declares an http/https data scheme; the only https schemes are inside <queries> elements of app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml.

The only BROWSABLE custom-scheme handlers are library activities (AppAuth RedirectUriReceiverActivity, MSAL BrowserTabActivity) used for OAuth redirects; the app has no custom URL scheme handler of its own. UriHandler only accepts content: URIs and isn't BROWSABLE.

cert4android's TrustCertificateActivity is exported with no permission and records a certificate trust decision taken from the intent (EXTRA_CERTIFICATE + EXTRA_TRUSTED). Any app can start it, and on a repeat delivery (singleInstance, onNewIntent) the attacker's certificate is saved as user-trusted without a tap. User-trusted certificates bypass hostname checks, so CalDAV/Tasks.org traffic, including Basic-auth credentials, can be intercepted.

evidence.detail: TrustCertificateActivity is exported with no android:permission.
A trust decision taken from the caller's intent extra is registered directly.

fills.reason: Both exported services (WearDataService, ComplicationUpdateService) are WearableListenerService subclasses bound by Google Play Services for Wear data-layer messages; ComplicationUpdateService only triggers a refresh. Other exported services require system permissions (BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE, BIND_APP_FUNCTION_SERVICE, DashClock permission).

PebbleService registers a context receiver for com.getpebble.action.app.RECEIVE with RECEIVER_EXPORTED and no permission, on every app start. Any installed app can send Pebble-formatted messages that complete or save tasks (MSG_COMPLETE_TASK, MSG_SAVE_TASK) and trigger task reads. Manifest receivers (FireReceiver checks for an explicit intent; system-event receivers) weren't found to act on untrusted extras.

evidence.detail: Receiver that modifies tasks is registered as exported with no sender permission.
Unauthenticated broadcast can save tasks.

fills.reason: The generated Tasks.org app password is copied to the clipboard with a plain ClipData and no EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE flag, so it appears in clipboard previews and stays readable by keyboards and clipboard managers.

evidence.detail: Clip is set without marking it sensitive.
Used for the password field of the new app-password dialog.

fills.reason: java.util.Random is used only for random reminder times and backup scheduling jitter; IVs and PKCE values use SecureRandom.
Security values (GCM IV, PKCE verifier) come from SecureRandom; no time-based values are used as tokens or keys in the Android code read.
The AndroidKeyStore AES key that encrypts stored account passwords is generated without setKeySize, so it gets the 128-bit default, which the test treats as insufficient.

evidence.detail: KeyGenParameterSpec built without setKeySize(256); AES defaults to 128 bits.

fills.reason: The only Cipher on Android is AES/GCM/NoPadding; no DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish. MD5 in Astrid2TaskProvider hashes tag names into IDs, not encryption.
The cipher transformation is AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random 12-byte IV; no ECB mode or bare "AES" transformation.
No KeyPairGenerator or asymmetric Keystore keys in Android code; the only Keystore key is a symmetric AES key.
The only provider named in getInstance calls is AndroidKeyStore (KeyStore and KeyGenerator); no BC or other explicit provider.

No KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure/isKeyguardSecure or BiometricManager.canAuthenticate call anywhere; the Keystore key protecting account passwords is created without checking for a secure lock screen.

evidence.detail: Key generated with no secure-lock-screen check anywhere in the app.

fills.reason: No BiometricPrompt or biometric API in the app's sources.
No BiometricPrompt in the app's sources.
No biometric-bound keys; setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment is never used.
No BiometricPrompt, so setConfirmationRequired is not used.
No user-authentication-bound keys; setUserAuthenticationParameters/ValidityDurationSeconds are never used.
The OkHttp client uses SSLContext.getInstance("TLS") with default protocols; no ConnectionSpec, tlsVersions, TLSv1/1.1 or setEnabledProtocols in app code.
The only http:// URLs in Android code are the 127.0.0.1 loopback OAuth redirect and XML namespace constants; none are used for remote communication.
No direct SSLSocket use in app code; TLS goes through OkHttp with a HostnameVerifier set.

The custom X509TrustManager (cert4android) trusts any certificate stored as user-trusted before checking the system store. Because the exported TrustCertificateActivity lets another app record that decision, a certificate can be trusted without real user validation.

evidence.detail: User-trusted certificates are accepted before system validation.
The trust decision can come from an external intent extra.

fills.reason: The HostnameVerifier returns true for any hostname when the leaf certificate is in the user-trusted store, so a user-trusted (or externally injected) certificate is valid for every host.

evidence.detail: Hostname mismatch is accepted when the certificate is user-trusted.

fills.reason: ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded is never called (grep over all sources), so the GMS security provider isn't updated before the app's TLS connections.

evidence.detail: TLS context created without updating the security provider first.

fills.reason: The release manifest sets no networkSecurityConfig (only the debug source set does), and no CertificatePinner is used in code, so even the developer's own endpoints are not pinned. User-chosen CalDAV servers can't be pinned, but the developer's own endpoints could be.

evidence.detail: Application element has no android:networkSecurityConfig in the release manifest.

fills.reason: The app has no native code of its own (no CMake/ndk-build or .so files in the project); native libraries come from dependencies and need the built APK to inspect.
No native code in the project; dependency .so files are only in the built APK, which Ward can't inspect.
The app checks Build.VERSION.SDK_INT in many places to use newer APIs (e.g. clipboard toasts, PendingIntent mutability).
Needs an SBOM generated from the Gradle build; Ward's dependency analyzer couldn't resolve 46 BOM/catalog-managed versions or transitive dependencies.

getSerializableExtra is only read in non-exported activities (SnoozeActivity, TagPickerActivity) and result intents from the app's own activities; the exported FilterSelectionActivity uses typed getParcelableExtra. No ObjectInputStream.
Pro entitlement (Inventory.hasPro) comes from cached purchase state; whether locally stored purchase data is trusted without integrity checks needs a deeper review of the billing code.

The exported TasksContentProvider (todoagenda URI) puts the caller's selection string straight into SQL via SupportSQLiteQueryBuilder and runs only `.sql`, dropping selectionArgs. A caller holding READ_TASKS can inject SQL (e.g. UNION SELECT) to read any table.

evidence.detail: Caller-controlled selection is concatenated into the raw SQL that rawQuery executes.

fills.reason: The phone app has no Play In-App Updates or backend minimum-version gate; the only version comparison is the Wear app checking the phone app's version for compatibility.

evidence.detail: Version is declared but nothing enforces a minimum version at runtime.

The signing keystore comes from external project properties (tasksStoreFile); its key size can only be checked on the signed APK.
StrictMode is only referenced in the debug source set (app/src/debug BuildSetup and Debug screen); the release BuildSetup does not use it.
No native code in the project; dependency native binaries can only be checked for debug symbols in the built APK.
The app has no native code of its own implementing security logic (no CMake/ndk-build or .so in the project).
R8 minification is enabled for release (isMinifyEnabled = true), but whether security-relevant logic stays readable can only be judged on the decompiled APK.
No root detection (su paths, test-keys, RootBeer, Play Integrity) anywhere in the app's sources; application start runs without any environment check.

evidence.detail: App start-up with no root detection anywhere in the app.

evidence.detail: App start-up with no debugger detection anywhere in the app.
